title: Portrait style consistency: the B2 team in one picture
question: Keep standalone portraits, or move to group-generated ones (or a hybrid)?

media.caption:
Standalone game portraits (top) against portraits cut from the two hires group shots, all framed the same way: face on Kenji's face box, 597x768.

Per character, standalone vs group (line, shading, colour, face, eyes; imgqa drift is CCIP to the game portrait, pass < 0.05):
- Eric: closest match. Ponytail, stubble and silver glasses held on both seeds; hair a little ashier, face a little older with more lines. Line and shading about the same as his standalone (it was already RDBT with this wording). Drift 0.025 / 0.034 pass. Glasses flagged on colour (dE 17-23, noisy on his silver frame per the calibration notes); the cut-out 'matte frame' fail sits where the approved portrait scores 0.80 too.
- Mio: most drift. Frames come out thin silver-grey rectangles, not her taupe rounded ones; eyes blue instead of light tan; lighter line than her heavy black ink; hair navy-black with a softer green. Drift 0.111 / 0.134 fail. Her frame would still need the transplant method.
- Kenji: his standalone has the heaviest outline and flat, saturated fill with orange skin, the biggest style outlier of the five. In the group he gets the shared medium line and grey shading, but his face is less round and babyish, stubble appears (his own negative had stubble/facial hair; the shared one didn't) and his forearms are muscular. Drift 0.068 warn / 0.090 fail.
- Mr. Mori: standalone has fine hatching, deep lines and warm brown skin (and holds a tea cup). Group: cleaner, fewer wrinkles, looks younger; glasses added on both seeds though he has none; empty hands. Drift 0.109 fail / 0.076 warn.
- Emi: standalone is glossy with auburn-red hair and a big open smile. Group: plain brown hair, softer smile; 1001 lost her glasses, 1003 kept them. Drift 0.061 warn / 0.110 fail.
Overall: the group row is the more consistent set: one line weight, one cool-grey shadow colour, the same eye drawing, skin palette and light. The standalone row mixes heavy ink (Mio, Kenji), hatching (Mori), glossy soft shading (Emi) and Eric's cleaner line. The cost is identity: only Eric passes the drift check; the others lose named traits (Mio's frames and eye colour, Emi's auburn, Mori gains glasses, Kenji gains stubble).
Cut-out limits: where two people overlap there is a straight vertical cut and a sliver of the neighbour at the edge (Mio's left, Mori's left); a real run would space them apart in the collage. No red rim on any render (0 to 4%).
Layout collage used as the img2img start for c and later (not a render).

decision: Jørgen in chat, 2026-09-30: the original Mio and Kuro are his favourites; align the world's portrait style around those two (he expects it to be tough). Milden Mio's stylization a little. Make Kenji look less like a Miyazaki character.
